arxiv-2102-07255.title: Frequency prediction from exact or self-consistent meanflows
arxiv-2102-07255.creator: Yacine Bengana, Laurette S. Tuckerman
arxiv-2102-07255.description: Abstract A number of approximations have been proposed to estimate basic hydrodynamic quantities, in particular the frequency of a limit cycle. One of these, RZIF (for Real Zero Imaginary Frequency), calls for linearizing the governing equations about the mean flow and estimating the frequency as the imaginary part of the leading eigenvalue.

arxiv-2110-12515.title: Perturbation theory and linear partial differential equations with delay
arxiv-2110-12515.creator: Ismail T. Huseynov 1 , Nazim I. Mahmudov 1 1 Department of Mathematics, Eastern Mediterranean University, Mersin 10, 99628, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Turkey, e-mail adresses: i ​ s ​ m ​ a ​ i ​ l . h ​ u ​ s ​ e ​ y ​ n ​ o ​ v ​ @ ​ e ​ m ​ u . e ​ d ​ u . t ​ r ismail.huseynov@emu.edu.
arxiv-2110-12515.description: Abstract Functional evolution equations are used in the modeling of numerous physical processes. In this work, our main tool is perturbation theory of strongly continuous semigroups. The advantage of this technique is that one can provide functional evolution equations with the explicit representation formulas of the solution.

arxiv-2110-15381.title: Probing Hot Gas Components of Circumgalactic Medium in Cosmological Simulations with the Thermal Sunyaev-Zel’dovich Effect astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , numpy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , Mop-c GT (“Model-to-observable projection code for Galaxy Thermodynam
arxiv-2110-15381.creator: Junhan Kim, Sunil Golwala, James G. Bartlett, Stefania Amodeo, Nicholas Battaglia, Andrew J. Benson, J. Colin Hill, Philip F. Hopkins, Cameron B. Hummels, Emily Moser, Matthew E. Orr
arxiv-2110-15381.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Junhan Kim, Sunil Golwala, James G. Bartlett, Stefania Amodeo, Nicholas Battaglia, Andrew J. Benson, J. Colin Hill, Philip F. Hopkins, Cameron B. Hummels, Emily Moser, Matthew E. Orr. The thermal Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (tSZ) effect is a powerful tool with the potential for constraining directly the properties of the hot gas that dominates dark matter halos because it measures pressure and thus thermal energy density.

arxiv-2202-04565.title: Precision Radiotherapy via Information Integration of Expert Human Knowledge and AI Recommendation to Optimize Clinical Decision Making Journal: International Journal of Medical Informatics
arxiv-2202-04565.creator: Wenbo Sun, Dipesh Niraula, Issam El Naqa, Randall K Ten Haken, Ivo D Dinov, Kyle Cuneo, Judy (Jionghua) Jin
arxiv-2202-04565.description: Abstract In the precision medicine era, there is a growing need for precision radiotherapy where the planned radiation dose needs to be optimally determined by considering a myriad of patient-specific information in order to ensure treatment efficacy. Existing artificial-intelligence (AI) methods can recommend radiation dose prescriptions within the scope of this available information.

arxiv-2203-10033.title: Skill-based Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning of Industrial Robot Tasks with Planning and Knowledge Integration
arxiv-2203-10033.creator: Matthias Mayr, Faseeh Ahmad, Konstantinos Chatzilygeroudis, Luigi Nardi, Volker Krueger
arxiv-2203-10033.description: Abstract In modern industrial settings with small batch sizes it should be easy to set up a robot system for a new task. Strategies exist, e.g. the use of skills, but when it comes to handling forces and torques, these systems often fall short.

arxiv-2211-13415.title: JT gravity from holographic reduction of 3D asymptotically flat spacetime
arxiv-2211-13415.creator: Arindam Bhattacharjee, Muktajyoti Saha
arxiv-2211-13415.description: Abstract We attempt to understand the CFT 1 structure underlying (2+1)D gravity in flat spacetime via dimensional reduction. We observe that under superrotation, the hyperbolic (and dS 2 ) slices of flat spacetime transform to asymptotically (A)dS 2 slices. We consider a wedge region bounded by two such surfaces as End-of-the-World branes and employ Wedge holography to perform holographic reduction.

arxiv-2402-19028.title: Invariant Checking for SMT-based Systems with Quantifiers DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: ACM Transaction of Computational Logic; ; ACM Transaction of Computational Logic Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Theory of computation Verification by model checking CCS: Theory of computation
arxiv-2402-19028.creator: Gianluca Redondi, Alessandro Cimatti, Alberto Griggio, Kenneth McMillan
arxiv-2402-19028.description: Abstract . This paper addresses the problem of checking invariant properties for a large class of symbolic transition systems, defined by a combination of SMT theories and quantifiers. State variables can be functions from an uninterpreted sort (finite, but unbounded) to an interpreted sort, such as the the integers under the theory of linear arithmetic.

arxiv-2404-11875.title: Concept Induction using LLMs: A user experiment for assessment
arxiv-2404-11875.creator: Adrita Barua, Cara Widmer, Pascal Hitzler
arxiv-2404-11875.description: Abstract Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) poses a significant challenge in providing transparent and understandable insights into complex AI models. Traditional post-hoc algorithms, while useful, often struggle to deliver interpretable explanations. Concept-based models offer a promising avenue by incorporating explicit representations of concepts to enhance interpretability.

arxiv-2409-03194.title: Free circle actions on ( n − 1 ) (n-1) -connected ( 2 ​ n + 1 ) (2n+1) -manifolds
arxiv-2409-03194.creator: Yi Jiang, Yang Su
arxiv-2409-03194.description: Abstract In this paper, we determine those ( n − 1 ) (n-1) -connected ( 2 ​ n + 1 ) (2n+1) -manifolds with torsion free homology that admit free circle actions up to almost diffeomorphism, provided that n ≡ 5 , 7 mod 8 n\equiv 5,7\mod 8 .

arxiv-2501-08110.title: Underlying Physical Mechanisms in Upward Positive Flashes
arxiv-2501-08110.creator: T. Oregel-Chaumont, A. Šunjerga, J. Kasparian, M. Rubinstein, F. Rachidi
arxiv-2501-08110.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by T. Oregel-Chaumont, A. Šunjerga, J. Kasparian, M. Rubinstein, F. Rachidi. This study presents the first observation of a mixed mode of charge transfer during an upward positive flash, which was initiated from the Säntis Tower in Switzerland. High-speed camera footage, along with current and electric field measurements, revealed a downward-propagating recoil leader connecting to the grounded current-carrying plasma channel at a junction height of < < 1 km above the tip of the tower.

arxiv-2504-19452.title: Geometry-Informed Neural Operator Transformer
arxiv-2504-19452.creator: Qibang Liu, Vincient Zhong, Hadi Meidani, Diab Abueidda, Seid Koric, Philippe Geubelle
arxiv-2504-19452.description: Abstract Machine-learning-based surrogate models offer significant computational efficiency and faster simulations compared to traditional numerical methods, especially for problems requiring repeated evaluations of partial differential equations. This work introduces the Geometry-Informed Neural Operator Transformer (GINOT), which integrates the transformer architecture with the neural operator framework to enable forward predictions for arbitrary geometries.

arxiv-2505-24794.title: Cardinalities of the total number of independent sets
arxiv-2505-24794.creator: Benedek Kovács, Zoltán Lóránt Nagy
arxiv-2505-24794.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Benedek Kovács, Zoltán Lóránt Nagy. We study the set of numbers the total number of independent sets can admit in n n -vertex graphs. arxiv-2506-04870.title: Aligning Multimodal Representations through an Information Bottleneck
arxiv-2506-04870.creator: Antonio Almudévar, José Miguel Hernández-Lobato, Sameer Khurana, Ricard Marxer, Alfonso Ortega
arxiv-2506-04870.description: Abstract Contrastive losses have been extensively used as a tool for multimodal representation learning. However, it has been empirically observed that their use is not effective to learn an aligned representation space. In this paper, we argue that this phenomenon is caused by the presence of modality-specific information in the representation space.

arxiv-2510-22509.title: A Unified Study of Bohr’s Inequality for analytic and harmonic mappings on the Unit Disk
arxiv-2510-22509.creator: Molla Basir Ahamed, Partha Pratim Roy, Sujoy Majumder
arxiv-2510-22509.description: Abstract . We investigate improved forms of the Bohr inequality, using the quantity S r / π S_{r}/\pi , for analytic self-maps in class ℬ \mathcal{B} of 𝔻 \mathbb{D} , where S r S_{r} is the area measure of 𝔻 r \mathbb{D}_{r} .

arxiv-2601-23077.title: A Universal Convolution-Based Pre-processor to Correct the Prevalence-Incidence Gap in SIR, SEIR, and SIRS Modeling
arxiv-2601-23077.creator: José de Jesús Bernal-Alvarado, David Delepine
arxiv-2601-23077.description: Abstract Background: Traditional compartmental models, including SIR, SEIR, and SIRS frameworks, remain the analytical standard for epidemic forecasting. However, real-world data validation consistently reveals significant predictive failures, such as peak underestimations of up to 50%. Methods: This research identifies a persistent ”fundamental methodological error”: the calibration of prevalence-based (stock) models using raw daily incidence (flow) data without proper transformation.

arxiv-2602-15141.title: Mimicking the large-scale structure of the Local Universe
arxiv-2602-15141.creator: M. Alcázar-Laynez, S. Duarte Puertas, S. Verley, G. Blázquez-Calero, A. Jiménez, A. Lorenzo-Gutiérrez, D. Espada, M. Argudo-Fernández, I. Pérez

Pérez. Current observational and simulated large-scale structure (LSS) catalogues often lack consistency in assigning galaxies to specific structures, due to the absence of a universally accepted classification criterion.

pmc-10537520.title: Improving Sustainability through Covalent Adaptable Networks in the Recycling of Polyurethane Plastics
pmc-10537520.creator: Edoardo Miravalle, Pierangiola Bracco, Valentina Brunella, Claudia Barolo, Marco Zanetti
pmc-10537520.description: The global plastic waste problem has created an urgent need for the development of more sustainable materials and recycling processes. Polyurethane (PU) plastics, which represent 5.5% of globally produced plastics, are particularly challenging to recycle owing to their crosslinked structure. Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) based on dynamic covalent bonds have emerged as a promising solution for recycling PU waste.

pmc-10584005.title: Age But Not Menopausal Status Is Linked to Lower Resting Energy Expenditure
pmc-10584005.creator: Jari E Karppinen, Petri Wiklund, Johanna K Ihalainen, Hanna-Kaarina Juppi, Ville Isola, Matti Hyvärinen, Essi K Ahokas, Urho M Kujala, Jari Laukkanen, Juha J Hulmi, Juha P Ahtiainen, Sulin Cheng, Eija K Laakkonen
pmc-10584005.description: ContextIt remains uncertain whether aging before late adulthood and menopause are associated with fat-free mass and fat mass–adjusted resting energy expenditure (REEadj).ObjectivesWe investigated whether REEadj differs between middle-aged and younger women and between middle-aged women with different menopausal statuses. We repeated the age group comparison between middle-aged mothers and their daughters to partially control for genotype.

pmc-11672273.title: Controlling the Thermoelectric Performance of Doped Naphthobisthiadiazole‐Based Donor–Acceptor Conjugated Polymers through Backbone Engineering
pmc-11672273.creator: Jian‐Fa Ding, Kodai Yamanaka, Shao‐Huan Hong, Guan‐Lin Chen, Wei‐Ni Wu, Jhih‐Min Lin, Shih‐Huang Tung, Itaru Osaka, Cheng‐Liang Liu
pmc-11672273.description: This study investigates backbone engineering and evaluates the thermoelectric properties of FeCl3‐doped naphthobisthiadiazole (NTz)‐based donor–acceptor (D‐A) conjugated polymer films. The NTz acceptor unit is coupled with three distinct donor units, namely dialkylated terthiophene (3T), dialkylated quaterthiophene (4T), and dialkylated bisthienyl thienothiophene (2T‐TT) to yield copolymers designated as PNTz3T, PNTz4T, and PNTzTT.

pmc-12553296.title: Exploring knowledge, confidence and barriers to evidence-based practice implementation of self-management strategy for low back pain during chiropractic training in France: a mixed method study
pmc-12553296.creator: Sylvain Pigeon, Arnaud Lardon, André Bussières
pmc-12553296.description: IntroductionNon-specific low back pain (NSLBP), with or without radiation, is a leading cause of global disability. International guidelines recommend that healthcare providers extend self-management support (SMS) to patients to alleviate pain and disability. However, the adoption of SMS strategies remains suboptimal.

pmc-12729383.title: Integrated Genetic Characterization and Quantitative Risk Assessment of Cephalosporin- and Ciprofloxacin-Resistant Salmonella in Pork from Thailand
pmc-12729383.creator: Thawanrut Kiatyingangsulee, Si Thu Hein, Rangsiya Prathan, Songsak Srisanga, Saharuetai Jeamsripong, Rungtip Chuanchuen, Filip Gamoń, Suparna Mitra, Ewa Kotlarska
pmc-12729383.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: This study assessed the risk associated with third-generation cephalosporin- and fluoroquinolone-resistant Salmonella from pork consumption by integrating phenotypic resistance profiles with genetic data to characterize the risks and transmission pathways. Methods: Salmonella were isolated from raw pork meat samples (n = 793) collected from fresh markets and hypermarkets across Bangkok during 2021–2022, of which 150 were extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing and 31 were fluoroquinolone-resistant isolates. Phenotypic and genotypic resistance profiles were characterized.

pmc-12954684.title: A Social Media Single Session Intervention Designed to Promote Healthier Social Media Use: Youth Focus Group Feedback
pmc-12954684.creator: Jane Harness, Sarah E Domoff, Heide Rollings, Jessica L Schleider, Amaryllis Mavragani
pmc-12954684.description: BackgroundThe effects of social media use on an individual’s well- or ill-being are highly contextualized to the individual’s characteristics and their specific type of social media use. Youth have variable levels of insight about how social media affects them, knowledge about different ways they can change their use, and self-efficacy to make changes.

pmc-13210275.title: A Review of Embedded Artificial Intelligence Research (2023–2026): Technological Advancements, Representative Advances, and Future Prospects
pmc-13210275.creator: Zhaoyun Zhang
pmc-13210275.description: Since the publication of the “Review of Embedded Artificial Intelligence Research” in 2023, driven by innovations in hardware architectures, advances in lightweight algorithms, and the maturation of edge–cloud collaboration technologies, embedded artificial intelligence (embedded AI) has progressed from “technically feasible” to “large-scale deployment”.

pmc-13228940.title: Describing the use of ruxolitinib for the treatment of myelofibrosis: a plain language summary of the ROMEI early study results
pmc-13228940.creator: Massimo Breccia, Paola Guglielmelli, Chiara Castiglioni, Francesca Palandri, Francesco Passamonti
pmc-13228940.description: Plain Language Summary What is this summary about? This plain language summary describes the first results obtained from the ROMEI study. In this study, researchers want to learn how doctors in Italy use ruxolitinib to treat people with myelofibrosis, a rare type of blood cancer. It also looks at how ruxolitinib affects the symptoms and overall health of participants.

pmc-13237690.title: Factors of crisis and culture in international and Chinese death education research: a comparative bibliometric analysis
pmc-13237690.creator: Yufei Lin, Yan Liu, Jianting Cao, Ziping Pang, Xinran Song, Fangping Dang
pmc-13237690.description: IntroductionThe sensitive nature of mortality has hindered the death education. However, post-pandemic existential anxiety has drawn significant attention, offering a critical opportunity for disciplinary advancement. Despite this momentum, the field's interdisciplinary nature lacks a unified theoretical framework, urgently necessitating clear development directions.

pmc-13600115.title: Long-Term Survival of Very Elderly Patients with Heart Failure Managed in a Comprehensive Heart Failure Management Unit
pmc-13600115.creator: Sonia González-Sosa, Alba Rodríguez-Quintana, Pablo Santana-Vega, Jose A. Rodríguez-González, José M. García-Vallejo, Jorge Arencibia-Borrego, Alicia Conde-Martel
pmc-13600115.description: Background: Heart failure (HF) is the leading cause of hospitalisation in older adults, with incidence increasing markedly with age. However, long-term outcome data in patients aged ≥85 years remain limited. We evaluated survival and predictors of mortality in this very elderly HF population enrolled in a structured outpatient programme.

pmc-13672855.creator: Michael Heuser, Anna Dolnik, Isabell Arnhardt, Courteney K. Lai, Ekaterina Jahn, Mustafa Salim, Gudrun Göhring, Yvonne Lisa Behrens, Jonathan L. pmc-13672855.description: Key Points•Shallow long-read WGS provides high-resolution copy number variation profiles for karyotyping in patients with AML.•LcWGS delivers highly reproducible, sensitive, and prognostic information within 72 hours. Introduction Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a genetically diverse malignancy characterized by recurrent chromosomal abnormalities that not only drive leukemogenesis but also guide risk stratification and treatment decisions.
